Definition: {a horoscopist (as drawing magical lines or circles)}
BiblicalUsage: Chartom is the magician, the horoscopist who draws magical lines and circles, and Daniel's whole book is their undoing. The Chaldeans say no king has asked such things at any magician or astrologer or Chaldean, Daniel says the secret cannot be shown by the wise men, the astrologers, the magicians, or the soothsayers, and the magicians come in and cannot make the dream known. Nebuchadnezzar himself calls Belteshazzar the master of the magicians.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the magicians are in the book to fail: they are summoned four times and they fail four times, and Daniel succeeds because the God in heaven reveals secrets. I hold that every human art that claims to read the future is a poor copy of prophecy, and Babylon proves it.
